description: Demonstration images. Items marked synthetic are drawings generated by scripts/generate-demo.ts, not photographs; their ground truth is the drawn pixel area of each glass class, exact for the drawing but saying nothing about performance on real photographs. Items marked real are openly licensed photographs (CC BY-SA 3.0) with no measured ground truth.

items.title: Mixed fragments on a dark surface
items.description: SYNTHETIC image generated by code — not a photograph of real cullet. Clear, green and amber pieces spread on a dark grey surface.
items.limitations: Clear glass is drawn semi-transparent over grey, so it appears grey and may be partly classified as uncertain. Ideal, even lighting; no real optics (refraction, thickness, dirt).

items.title: Mostly green on a light surface
items.description: SYNTHETIC image generated by code — not a photograph of real cullet. Predominantly green fragments with some clear and amber on a pale neutral surface.
items.limitations: Clear glass on a pale neutral background is nearly the same colour as the background, so clear area is expected to be under-estimated — the app should flag this.

items.title: Packed pile filling the frame
items.description: SYNTHETIC image generated by code — not a photograph of real cullet. Densely overlapping fragments with dark gaps and no visible surface.
items.limitations: No background to separate, so individual fragments are not segmented (region-level analysis only). Dark gaps between pieces are counted as uncertain material. Uniform patches where clear pieces overlap can be flagged by the heuristic screening — an example of a false positive.

items.title: Fragments with non-glass look-alikes
items.description: SYNTHETIC image generated by code — not a photograph of real cullet. Mixed glass plus drawn stand-ins for a ceramic chip, a metal cap, a blue plastic piece and a dark stone.
items.limitations: The foreign objects are simple drawn shapes with idealised appearance. Detecting them here does not show that real ceramic, metal, plastic or stone would be detected.

items.title: Underexposed and blurred
items.description: SYNTHETIC image generated by code — not a photograph of real cullet. The mixed scene, darkened and blurred to imitate a poor photograph.
items.limitations: Deliberately poor image. The expected outcome is that the app reports the image as unsuitable or low-reliability.

items.title: Real photo — mixed colours
items.description: Real photograph of washed, re-sorted cullet from a glass processing plant on white paper, with a €1 coin for scale (Wikimedia Commons, 2009). Mixed clear, green, amber and blue pieces, plus a few small light-coloured non-glass-looking bits.
items.limitations: Top lighting makes thick dark glass appear near-black, so much of it is uncertain. The paper background is neutral, so clear glass is hard to separate. The pile is one connected mass, so fragments merge. No measured composition exists for this photo.
items.expectation: Visibly mixed; the uploader describes it as various colours. No measured composition.

attribution.changes: Downscaled to 1280×960 by Wikimedia's thumbnail service; no other changes.

items.title: Real photo — sorted green
items.description: Real photograph of washed, re-sorted cullet from a glass processing plant on white paper, with a €1 coin for scale (Wikimedia Commons, 2009). Labelled by the uploader as the green fraction.
items.limitations: Thick dark-green pieces are near-black under top lighting and become uncertain. Includes olive-toned pieces that sit near the green/brown hue boundary.
items.expectation: Predominantly green by the uploader's sorting label. Not a measured composition.

attribution.author: Alter Fritz (Wikimedia Commons)
attribution.changes: Downscaled to 1280×960 by Wikimedia's thumbnail service; no other changes.

items.title: Real photo — sorted amber
items.description: Real photograph of washed, re-sorted cullet from a glass processing plant on white paper, with a €1 coin for scale (Wikimedia Commons, 2009). Labelled by the uploader as the amber (brown) fraction.
items.limitations: Much of the pile is near-black and therefore uncertain. The €1 coin is real metal and is not flagged by the screening in this photo, while some glass glints may be — an example of both false negatives and false positives.
items.expectation: Predominantly brown/amber by the uploader's sorting label. Not a measured composition.

items.title: Real photo — sorted clear (flint)
items.description: Real photograph of washed, re-sorted cullet from a glass processing plant on white paper, with a €1 coin for scale (Wikimedia Commons, 2009). Labelled by the uploader as the white (clear/flint) fraction.
items.limitations: Clear glass transmits the white paper, so separating it from the background is unreliable; light-green-tinted pieces fall into the uncertain band.
items.expectation: Predominantly clear by the uploader's sorting label. Not a measured composition.

items.title: Real photo — sorted blue
items.description: Real photograph of washed, re-sorted cullet from a glass processing plant on white paper, with a €1 coin for scale (Wikimedia Commons, 2009). Labelled by the uploader as the blue fraction, which also contains clear pieces.
items.limitations: Blue glass is outside the three main classes, so it is reported as 'other colour' and triggers 'unusual colour' flags by design — those flags do not mean the pieces are contaminants.
items.expectation: Blue plus clear pieces by the uploader's label. Not a measured composition.
